title: Why Are the St. Louis Blues Named After a Song?
description:
Watching Stars vs. Blues? St. Louis's NHL team is named after W. C. Handy's 1914 song "The St. Louis Blues", and it took a very different song to finally win the Stanley Cup.

Every frame is drawn with code. No stock footage, no AI video.

0:15 "A heart like a rock cast in the sea"

A note on the story: in his autobiography (Father of the Blues, 1941), W. C. Handy wrote that while he was broke in St. Louis in 1892, sleeping on the cobblestones of the Mississippi levee, he passed a woman who muttered "Ma man's got a heart like a rock cast in de sea"; years later, writing in Memphis, that memory set the mood of the song he named the St. Louis Blues (published by Pace & Handy, 1914). The NHL's 1967 expansion added six teams to the Original Six; owners Sid Salomon Jr. and Sid Salomon III named the St. Louis franchise after Handy's song. The Blues reached the Stanley Cup Final in 1968, 1969 and 1970 and were swept each time. In January 2019 they were last in the NHL; after some players heard Laura Branigan's "Gloria" at a South Philadelphia bar, it became the team's victory song, and that June they won their first Stanley Cup.

Images: "The Saint Louis Blues" sheet-music cover (Pace & Handy Music Co., Memphis, 1914; Wikimedia Commons, public domain). St. Louis Blues sheet music, interior page (University of Alberta sheet music collection via the Internet Archive, public domain). The Stanley Cup, music notes and maps are drawn in code; maps from Natural Earth (world-atlas) and US Census (us-atlas) outlines.
Sources: W. C. Handy, "Father of the Blues: An Autobiography" (1941); St. Louis Blues team history (NHL.com, Britannica); Stanley Cup Final results 1968-1970 and 2019 (NHL.com); "Play Gloria" (NHL.com, CBC, WHYY, 2019).
Narration voice is synthetic.
